newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures close lower in all months.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures close lower in all months.

text.p: All Tokyo corn futures ended lower on Tuesday, as the Chicago market's price losses overnight offset the weaker yen against the dollar, traders said.
Prices were 30 to 90 yen lower, with the benchmark January 1998 contract down 90 yen at 14,870 yen per tonne. The day's volume was 66,863 lots.
Active selling by individual investors depressed all months from the opening, but light technical buying emerged in the afternoon, traders said.
The Chicago soybean market fell overnight on rain in Brazil, a major soy producer, and this helped push down the Chicago corn market.
"We'll continue to watch weather conditions in South America," a brokerage house trader said.
The spot March corn contract on the CBOT Project A trading system was being traded at $2.71-3/4 per bushel at 0740 GMT, unchanged from Monday's close.
The spot January for CBOT soybean futures on the overnight trading system was at $7.42 at 0740 GMT, down from $7.44-1/2 at Monday's close.--Tokyo Commodities Desk +81-3-3432-7391
